plan: Zechariah 9:1-8, 9-17; Zechariah 10:1–11:3; Zechariah 11:4-17; Zechariah 12:1-14; Zechariah 13:1-6, 7-9; Zechariah 14:1-21

readings.title: Oracle Against Hadrach and Damascus
readings.subtitle: The Pride of the Philistines Cut Off
readings.text: [Zechariah 9:1] The message of the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> against the land of Ḥaḏraḵ, and Dammeseq its resting place – when the eye of man and all the tribes of Yisra’ěl are on <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – [2] and Ḥamath also borders on it, Tsor and Tsiḏon, though they are very wise. [3] For Tsor built herself a tower, heaped up silver like the dust, and gold like the mud of the streets. [4] See, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall dispossess her, and <dn>He</dn> shall strike her power in the sea, and she shall be consumed by fire. [5] Ashqelon sees it and fears, Azzah too, writhing in anguish, and Eqron, for her expectation has dried up. And the sovereign shall perish from Azzah, and Ashqelon shall not be inhabited. [6] <dq>“And a mamzer shall settle in Ashdoḏ. So <dn>I</dn> shall cut off <dn>את</dn> the pride of the Philistines,</dq> [7] <dq>and shall take away <dn>את</dn> his blood from his mouth, and the abominations from between his teeth. And he shall remain, even he, to our <dn>Elohim</dn>, and he shall be like a leader in Yehuḏah, and Eqron like a Yeḇusite.</dq> [8] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall encamp around <dn>My</dn> house, against an army, against him who passes by and him who returns, so that no oppressor passes through them again, for now <dn>I</dn> have seen with <dn>My</dn> eyes.”</dq>

readings.title: The King Comes on a Donkey
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH Will Save His People
readings.text: [Zechariah 9:9] <dq>“Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Tsiyon! Shout, O daughter of Yerushalayim! See, your Sovereign is coming to you, <dn>He</dn> is righteous and endowed with deliverance, humble and riding on a donkey, a colt, the foal of a donkey.</dq> [10] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall cut off <dn>את</dn> the chariot from Ephrayim and <dn>את</dn> the horse from Yerushalayim. And the battle bow shall be cut off. And <dn>He</dn> shall speak peace to the nations, and <dn>His</dn> rule is from sea to sea, and from the River to the ends of the earth.</dq> [11] <dq>“Also you, because of the blood of your covenant, <dn>I</dn> shall send your prisoners out of the pit.</dq> [12] <dq>“Return to the stronghold, you prisoners of the expectation. Even today <dn>I</dn> declare that <dn>I</dn> return double to you.</dq> [13] <dq>“For <dn>I</dn> shall bend <dn>את</dn> Yehuḏah for <dn>Me</dn>, <dn>I</dn> shall fill the bow with <dn>את</dn> Ephrayim, and <dn>I</dn> shall stir up your sons, O Tsiyon, against your sons, O Greece, and <dn>I</dn> shall make you like the sword of a mighty man.”</dq> [14] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall appear for them, and <dn>His</dn> arrow go forth like lightning, and the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sound with the shophar. And <dn>He</dn> shall go with whirlwinds from the south, [15] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts shall shield them. And they shall devour and trample on sling stones. And they shall drink, roar as if with wine, and they shall be filled like basins, like the corners of the slaughter-place. [16] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn> shall save them in that day, as the flock of <dn>His</dn> people, for the stones of a diadem, sparkling over <dn>His</dn> land. [17] For what goodness is <dn>His</dn>, and what comeliness is <dn>His</dn>. Grain make the young men thrive, and new wine the maidens!

readings.title: YeHoVaH Will Restore His Flock
readings.subtitle: Judgment on False Shepherds and Lebanon's Fall
readings.text: [Zechariah 10:1] Ask <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for rain in the time of the latter rain, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who makes storm clouds. And <dn>He</dn> gives them showers of rain, the plants in the field to everyone. [2] For the household idols spoke emptiness, the diviners saw falsehood, and relate dreams of deceit, they comfort in vain. Therefore they have wandered about like sheep. They are afflicted, for there is no shepherd. [3] <dq>“<dn>My</dn> wrath burns against the shepherds, and <dn>I</dn> lay a charge against the leaders. For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts shall visit <dn>His</dn> flock, the house of Yehuḏah, and make them like <dn>His</dn> splendid horse in battle.</dq> [4] <dq>“From him comes the corner-stone, from him the tent peg, from him the battle bow, from him every ruler, together.</dq> [5] <dq>“And they shall be like mighty men, who trample down the mud of the streets in the battle. And they shall fight because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is with them, and the riders on horses shall be put to shame.</dq> [6] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall make the house of Yehuḏah mighty, and save the house of Yosěph. And <dn>I</dn> shall bring them back, because <dn>I</dn> have compassion on them. And they shall be as though <dn>I</dn> had not pushed them aside. For <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>, and <dn>I</dn> answer them.</dq> [7] <dq>“And Ephrayim shall be as a mighty man, and their heart shall rejoice as if with wine. And their children shall see and rejoice, their heart exulting in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [8] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall whistle for them and gather them, for <dn>I</dn> shall ransom them. And they shall increase as they once increased.</dq> [9] <dq>“Though <dn>I</dn> sow them among peoples, they shall remember <dn>Me</dn> in places far away. And they shall live, together with their children, and they shall return.</dq> [10] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall bring them back from the land of Mitsrayim, and gather them from Ashshur, and bring them into the land of Gil‛aḏ and Leḇanon, until no more room is found for them.</dq> [11] <dq>“And <dn>He</dn> shall pass through the sea of distress, and strike the waves of the sea, and all the depths of the River shall dry up. And the pride of Ashshur shall be brought down, and the sceptre of Mitsrayim be taken away.</dq> [12] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall make them mighty in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, so that they walk up and down in <dn>His</dn> Name,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [Zechariah 11:1] Open your doors, O Leḇanon, and let fire devour your cedars. [2] Howl, O cypress, for the cedar has fallen, because the mighty are ravaged. Howl, O oaks of Bashan, for the dense forest has come down. [3] Listen! The howling of shepherds, for their splendour is ravaged. Listen! The roaring of lions, for the pride of the Yarděn is ravaged.

readings.title: The Shepherd and the Flock for Slaughter
readings.subtitle: Thirty Pieces of Silver
readings.text: [Zechariah 11:4] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>my</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dq>“Feed <dn>את</dn> the flock for slaughter,</dq> [5] <dq>whose owners kill them and feel no guilt, and their sellers say, ‘Blessed be <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for <dn>I</dn> have become rich.’ And their own shepherds do not spare them.</dq> [6] <dq>“For <dn>I</dn> shall no longer spare <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of the land,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>“But see, <dn>I</dn> am delivering up <dn>את</dn> mankind, each one into his neighbour’s hand and into the hand of his sovereign. And they shall crush <dn>את</dn> the earth, but <dn>I</dn> do not deliver from their hand.”</dq> [7] So I shepherded <dn>את</dn> the flock meant for slaughter, the truly poor of the flock. And I took for myself two staffs, the one I called Pleasantness, and the other I called Unity, and I shepherded <dn>את</dn> the flock. [8] Then I sent off <dn>את</dn> the three shepherds in one month, for my being despised them, and their being also loathed me. [9] So I said, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am not shepherding you. Let the dying die, and the straying stray, and let those who are left eat each other’s flesh.”</dq> [10] And I took <dn>את</dn> my staff, Pleasantness, and cut it in two, to break <dn>את</dn> the covenant which I had made with <dn>את</dn> all the peoples. [11] So it was broken on that day. And the poor of the flock, who were watching me, knew that it was the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [12] And I said to them, “If it is good in your eyes, give me my wages. And if not, refrain.” So they weighed out for my wages thirty pieces of silver. [13] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>“Throw it to the potter,”</dq> the splendid price at which I was valued by them. And I took <dn>את</dn> the thirty pieces of silver and threw them into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for the potter. [14] Then I cut in two <dn>את</dn> my other staff, Unity, to break <dn>את</dn> the brotherhood between Yehuḏah and Yisra’ěl. [15] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>“Take again <dn>את</dn> the implements of a foolish shepherd.</dq> [16] <dq>“For look, <dn>I</dn> am raising up a shepherd in the land who does not visit those straying, nor seek the young, nor heal those that are broken, nor feed those that still stand. But he does eat <dn>את</dn> the flesh of the fat and tear off their hooves.</dq> [17] <dq>“Woe to the worthless shepherd forsaking the flock! Let a sword be upon his arm and upon his right eye! His arm shall wither and his right eye shall be dimmed.”</dq>

readings.title: Jerusalem, a Cup of Reeling
readings.subtitle: Mourning for the One They Pierced
readings.text: [Zechariah 12:1] The message of the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> against Yisra’ěl. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, stretching out the heavens, and laying the foundation of the earth, and forming the spirit of man within him, declares, [2] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am making <dn>את</dn> Yerushalayim a cup of reeling to all the people all around, and also against Yehuḏah it is in the siege against Yerushalayim.</dq> [3] <dq>“And in that day it shall be that <dn>I</dn> make <dn>את</dn> Yerushalayim a very heavy stone for all peoples – all lifting it are severely injured. And all the nations of the earth shall be gathered against it.</dq> [4] <dq>“In that day,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> strike every horse with bewilderment and its rider with madness. And on the house of Yehuḏah <dn>I</dn> open <dn>My</dn> eyes, but every horse of the peoples <dn>I</dn> strike with blindness.</dq> [5] <dq>“And the leaders of Yehuḏah shall say in their heart, ‘The inhabitants of Yerushalayim are a strength to me, through <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, their <dn>Elohim</dn>.’</dq> [6] <dq>“In that day <dn>I</dn> make <dn>את</dn> the leaders of Yehuḏah like a fire pot among trees, and like a torch of fire in the sheaves. And they shall consume <dn>את</dn> all the peoples all around, on the right and on the left. And Yerushalayim shall dwell again in her own place, in Yerushalayim.</dq> [7] <dq>“And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall save <dn>את</dn> the tents of Yehuḏah first, so that the comeliness of the house of Daviḏ and the comeliness of the inhabitants of Yerushalayim would not become greater than that of Yehuḏah.</dq> [8] <dq>“In that day <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall shield the inhabitants of Yerushalayim. And the feeble among them in that day shall be like Daviḏ, and the house of Daviḏ like <dn>Elohim</dn>, like the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> before them!</dq> [9] <dq>“And it shall be in that day that <dn>I</dn> seek to destroy <dn>את</dn> all the nations that come against Yerushalayim.</dq> [10] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall pour on the house of Daviḏ and on the inhabitants of Yerushalayim a spirit of favour and prayers. And they shall look on <dn>Me</dn> whom they pierced, and they shall mourn for <dn>Him</dn> as one mourns for his only son. And they shall be in bitterness over <dn>Him</dn> as a bitterness over the first-born.</dq> [11] <dq>“In that day the mourning in Yerushalayim is going to be great, like the mourning at Haḏaḏ Rimmon in the valley of Meḡiddo.</dq> [12] <dq>“And the land shall mourn, every clan by itself: the clan of the house of Daviḏ by itself, and their women by themselves; the clan of the house of Nathan by itself, and their women by themselves;</dq> [13] <dq>the clan of the house of Lěvi by itself, and their women by themselves; the clan of Shim‛i by itself, and their women by themselves;</dq> [14] <dq>all the rest of the clans, every clan by itself, and their women by themselves.</dq>

readings.title: A Fountain Opened for Cleansing
readings.subtitle: Idols and False Prophets Removed
readings.text: [Zechariah 13:1] <dq>“In that day a fountain shall be opened for the house of Daviḏ and for the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, for sin and for uncleanness.</dq> [2] <dq>“And it shall be in that day,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>“that <dn>I</dn> cut off <dn>את</dn> the names of the idols from the earth, and they shall be remembered no more, and <dn>I</dn> shall also remove <dn>את</dn> the prophets and <dn>את</dn> the unclean spirit from the earth.</dq> [3] <dq>“And it shall be, when one prophesies again, then his father and mother who brought him forth shall say to him, ‘You shall not live, because you have spoken falsehood in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ And his father and mother who brought him forth shall pierce him through when he prophesies.</dq> [4] <dq>“And it shall be in that day that the prophets shall be ashamed, everyone of his vision when he prophesies, and not put a hairy robe on in order to deceive,</dq> [5] <dq>but shall say, ‘<dn>I</dn> am no prophet, <dn>I</dn> am a farmer, for a man sold me as a slave in my youth.’</dq> [6] <dq>“And one shall say to him, ‘What are these wounds in your hands?’ And he shall say, ‘Because <dn>I</dn> was struck at home by those who love me.’</dq>

readings.subsection: The Shepherd Struck, The Sheep Scattered
readings.title: The Shepherd Struck
readings.subtitle: A Remnant Refined
readings.text: [Zechariah 13:7] <dq>“O sword, awake against <dn>My</dn> Shepherd, against the Man who is <dn>My</dn> Companion,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts. <dq>“Strike <dn>את</dn> the Shepherd, and let the sheep be scattered. But <dn>I</dn> shall turn <dn>My</dn> hand upon the little ones.</dq> [8] <dq>And it shall be throughout all the soil,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“that two thirds therein are cut off and die, and one third is left therein.</dq> [9] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall bring <dn>את</dn> the third into fire, and refine them as silver is refined, and try them as gold is tried. They shall call on <dn>My</dn> Name, and <dn>I</dn> shall answer them. <dn>I</dn> shall say, ‘This is <dn>My</dn> people,’ while they say, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is my <dn>Elohim</dn>.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Final Battle and the Reign of YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: All Nations to Worship at Jerusalem
readings.text: [Zechariah 14:1] See, a day shall come for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and your spoil shall be divided in your midst. [2] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall gather <dn>את</dn> all the nations to battle against Yerushalayim. And the city shall be taken, the houses plundered, and the women ravished. Half of the city shall go into exile, but the remnant of the people shall not be cut off from the city.</dq> [3] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall go forth, and <dn>He</dn> shall fight against those nations, as <dn>He</dn> fights in the day of battle. [4] And in that day <dn>His</dn> feet shall stand upon the Mount of Olives, which faces Yerushalayim on the east. And the Mount of Olives shall be split in two, from east to west, a very great valley, and half of the mountain shall move toward the north and half of it toward the south. [5] And you shall flee to the valley of <dn>My</dn> mountain – for the valley of the mountains reaches to Atsal. And you shall flee as you fled from the earthquake in the days of Uzziyah sovereign of Yehuḏah. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>my</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> shall come – all the set-apart ones with You. [6] And in that day it shall be: there is no light, it is dark. [7] And it shall be one day which is known to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, neither day nor night, but at evening time there shall be light. [8] And in that day it shall be that living waters flow from Yerushalayim, half of them toward the eastern sea and half of them toward the western sea, in summer as well as in winter. [9] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall be Sovereign over all the earth. In that day there shall be one <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>His</dn> Name one. [10] All the land shall be changed into a desert plain from Geḇa to Rimmon south of Yerushalayim, and she shall be raised up and inhabited in her place from Binyamin’s Gate to the place of the First Gate and the Corner Gate, and from the Tover of Ḥanan’ěl to the winepresses of the sovereign. [11] And they shall dwell in her, and there shall be no more utter destruction, but Yerushalayim shall be safely inhabited. [12] And this is the plague with which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> plagues <dn>את</dn> all the people who fought against Yerushalayim: their flesh shall decay while they stand on their feet, and their eyes decay in their sockets, and their tongues decay in their mouths. [13] And it shall be in that day that a great confusion from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is among them, and everyone of them shall seize the hand of his neighbour, and his hand rise up against his neighbour’s hand. [14] And Yehuḏah shall fight at Yerushalayim as well. And the wealth of all the nations round about shall be gathered together: gold, and silver, and garments in great quantities. [15] So also is the plague on the horse and the mule, on the camel and the donkey, and on all the cattle that are in those camps – as this plague. [16] And it shall be that all who are left from all the nations which came up against Yerushalayim, shall go up from year to year to bow themselves to the Sovereign, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, and to celebrate the Festival of Sukkot. [17] And it shall be, that if anyone of the clans of the earth does not come up to Yerushalayim to bow himself to the Sovereign, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, on them there is to be no rain. [18] And if the clan of Mitsrayim does not come up and enter in, then there is no rain. On them is the plague with which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> plagues the nations who do not come up to celebrate the Festival of Sukkot. [19] This is the punishment of Mitsrayim and the punishment of all the nations that do not come up to celebrate the Festival of Sukkot. [20] In that day “SET-APART TO <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>" shall be engraved on the bells of the horses. And the pots in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall be like the bowls before the slaughter-place. [21] And every pot in Yerushalayim and Yehuḏah shall be set-apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts. And all those who slaughter shall come and take them and cook in them. And there shall no longer be a merchant in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, in that day.
